verdict: NEW places/pakistan (primary). Reason: the report is substantive and unique (a full map of Pakistan's federal/provincial/local property-related levies with rates, the valuation-base transition, land-record coverage by province, and recommendations), the wiki has no Pakistan page and no other Pakistan property-tax source, and the report is Tier 1 institutional. Optional companion NEW research/lucas-mas-touqeer-pakistan-immovable-property-tax (house convention is one research page per source, e.g. research/world-bank-property-tax-determinants); the places page should carry the content and the research page stay short. Not an LVT case: the page must frame Pakistan as a property-tax-administration and valuation-base-transition case (annual rental value to capital value), not as land value taxation. SUGGESTED SECTIONS for places/pakistan.md (follow places/nigeria.md pattern): Overview (lead: recurrent property tax is tiny, UIPT about 0.13 percent of GDP vs 0.3-0.6 / 1.2 percent benchmarks; heavy reliance on transaction taxes); The Tax Map (three taxable events: transfer, ownership, use; federal vs provincial vs local; short table of main levies and rates: stamp duty, CVT, registration/mutation, TTIP, advance taxes, capital gains, deemed rental income s.7E, UIPT, rental income tax, agricultural income tax and land tax); The Urban Immovable Property Tax and the Move from Rental Value to Capital Value (ARV base, exemptions, Punjab Jan 2025 DC-rate capital value with Rs5m exemption, Sindh devolution to local councils Sept 2024, other provinces agreed to follow); Valuation (three tables/two sets of rates, FBR 80 percent rule of thumb, DC rates below FBR, infrequent updating, informal-transfer effect); Land Records and Cadastre (Punjab digitised; KP half; Balochistan 5 percent; Sindh two-thirds of urban properties missing; Karachi survey 2001); Recommendations and Roadmap (rec 1-8, independent valuation agency, 3-5 year table updates, ratio studies, AVMs on pilot basis, merge CVT/stamp duty; the two roadmap tables; state that the report gives no dates); What the Report Does Not Say (see uncertainties/limits below; this section is the guard against overclaiming); See Also; Sources. INBOUND LINK CANDIDATES (>=2): (a) research/world-bank-property-tax-determinants, 'Bears On' or a See Also bullet: Pakistan as a case where the binding constraint is valuation and land-record administration; (b) concepts/mass-appraisal-methods, section 'The Failure Mode Isn't Bad Models - It's Rolls Nobody Updates', insert a short paragraph after the three-bullet list (last bullet begins 'Appeals redistribute rather than correct') and before the paragraph beginning 'The political economy of the fix is the discouraging part': Pakistan's valuation tables not updated regularly and set by incremental uplifts, with the report's recommendation of 3-5 year updates and sales-assessment ratio studies [grep: after every 3-5 years; incremental approach]; (c) research/brockmeyer-property-tax-developing, See Also / Bears On: enforcement/compliance context (report ties higher transfer taxes to informal transfers) - weaker link, use only as a see-also; (d) research/imf-taxing-immovable-property and research/franzsen-mccluskey-property-tax-africa, See Also (comparative administration); (e) events/telangana-cure-bill-hyderabad, See Also, as a South Asian contrast: both move off annual rental value, but Telangana's proposal moves to land value while Pakistan's moves to capital value of land plus buildings (this contrast is the useful one to state); (f) objections/land-cannot-be-assessed (only if the page states the report's land-record findings carefully as an administrative-capacity point). There is no places/india.md and no other South Asian places page (places has no India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal). Also optionally the new page could link concepts/site-value and concepts/split-rate-taxation to show what Pakistan has NOT adopted.
claim_grade: A for the statutory rates, tax map and administrative facts the report states from law and official practice (tables 1-24 etc.); B for provincial administrative-coverage figures (land-record coverage, 'two thirds of urban properties', 60-65 percent of KP outside tax net) which are attributed to no dated source in the text (footnote 6 cites World Bank 2020 SCD) and for the 0.13 percent of GDP UIPT figure (no year or citation given); C for recommendations and the 80 percent FBR rule of thumb (the report itself says it is not clear the table-update process uses verifiable data), and for the claim that revised FBR tables 'increased informal property transfers' (the report says 'it is said to have', relaying BoR representatives). Source tier: Tier 1 (World Bank is an official/standing body under EDITORIAL 4c). Caveats: the report carries the standard disclaimer that findings are not necessarily the Bank's views, and the authors are World Bank staff, so cite it as 'a World Bank report' with the authors named and avoid 'the World Bank recommends' for statements that are the authors' own.

uncertainties: WHAT THE REPORT DOES NOT SAY ABOUT LAND VALUE TAXATION (for the 'What the Report Does Not Say' section; the page must not overclaim): (1) It never recommends a land value tax, a site value tax, split-rate taxation or taxing land separately from buildings; the recommended base is capital value (land plus buildings, DC-rate-based in Punjab). Grep of the text for 'land value', 'site value', 'unimproved', 'vacant', 'Georg' finds no recommendation. (2) The only appearances of land or site as a base are the three classificatory annexes (Annex 1-3, report p.25-26): a 'Land (Site) Tax' is listed as one possible tax base among seven, 'Neutral' in rate structure and 'Unrealized value', valued 'Area basis' by a cost approach; the report does not say Pakistan has or should adopt it. (3) Vacant land: UIPT applies to vacant plots 'in some provinces' (p.14) and the report lists 'challenges in capturing value appreciation of vacant plots' (p.4) and omission of undeveloped land and vacant buildings from rolls, but proposes no specific vacant-land measure. (4) There is no analysis of tax incidence, capitalisation, land-price effects, windfall or speculation, rent capture, or of the distinction between land and improvement value; the nearest statement is rec 8's remark that recurrent taxes would 'relieve the higher tax burden on land and real estate transactions and encourage more productive use of land and property assets' (p.22) - a transfer-tax-to-recurrent-tax argument, not an LVT argument. (5) 'Land tax' in the report means the agricultural land tax (Balochistan, Punjab, KP: per-acre presumptive tax by productivity zone, alternative minimum tax for agricultural income tax), not a land value tax; the 'land value' phrase appears only for the land-use conversion fee (percentage of the uplift from agricultural to commercial value, p.19). That fee is a partial betterment-type capture and could be mentioned with that limitation, but the report does not call it value capture. (6) 'Value capture' appears only in recommendation 1 ('real time value capture' by shifting from ARV to CV), a generic phrase.

The roadmap has no dates, phases or sequencing: it is two activity/deliverable/objective tables (tax administration p.23; tax policy p.24). The only timing language is 'short- to medium-term' (exec summary), 'in the medium term' (rec 8), 'in short term' (rec 2) and 'after every 3-5 years' (table updates). The 2025-2035 Country Partnership Framework mentioned in the triage blurb is NOT in this report. Do not invent phases or dates; the brief's request for dates cannot be met from this source.

Recurrent property tax share of GDP: the only Pakistan figure is UIPT at 'about 0.13 percent of GDP' with no year or source; no total for all recurrent property taxes (deemed income tax, rental income tax, AIT, land tax are not totalled), no revenue figures for stamp duty, CVT or capital gains tax. The benchmarks (0.3-0.6 and 1.2 percent) are unsourced in the text. Treat as the authors' statement.

Deemed income tax: the report cites it as Sec. 7E of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 (introduced by Finance Act 2022), not 'Income Tax Ordinance 2022'. The report says the tax is owner-level, 20 percent of 5 percent of fair market value (so an effective 1 percent of FMV by simple arithmetic; the report does not state this, so any 1 percent figure would be a derived calculation to be labelled as such), on properties exceeding PKR 25 million. The report does not explain how the PKR 25 million threshold is measured. Rate/threshold are as of the report date and the federal budget changes them yearly.

Capital value tax: the report treats CVT as a provincial tax (taxing right provincial, BoR-administered, buyer-paid, on the higher of declared or DC-assessed value) levied at transfer, not the older federal CVT; in Punjab it is combined with stamp duty into a 2 percent charge. Table 6 (stamp duty) and Table 10 (CVT) each show Punjab at 1 percent; the text says the Punjab stamp duty rate 'includes CVT'. State the combined 2 percent with the text as authority and flag the table ambiguity if the table is cited.

Internal inconsistency to avoid: p.4 describes UIPT as ARV-based, then p.14 says ARV in all provinces except Punjab; Punjab's capital-value system took effect January 2025. The report says Sindh transferred UIPT collection to local councils in September 2024 and AIT administration to the Sindh Revenue Board in 2025. These legal changes are as of the report's date (revised 20 May 2026) and should be dated on the page ('as of the report's 2026 revision').

Stated uncertainty in the source: the text says the FBR 80 percent rule of thumb, the use of private property websites and the table-update process are not clearly documented; and that raising federal advance taxes is claimed by BoR representatives to have increased informal transactions. These are relayed assertions, not measured effects; phrase them that way.

The report is a policy diagnostic by two World Bank staff with a disclaimer that views are not necessarily the Bank's; it relies on roundtable presentations by provincial departments (Oct 2024, Feb 2025) and on World Bank 2020 SCD, not on published datasets. No independent verification of provincial figures was attempted. Source format caveat: pdftotext -layout interleaves the two text columns, so quote verification should rely on the short grep fragments given; if a quotation must be exact, check it against the PDF (pdftotext without -layout keeps column order, e.g. pdftotext -f 17 -l 17).
